    <item>
      <title>Nusa-dobbel for Leipzig i Meisterligaen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <description>Karoline Grøtting var best av samtlige kvinner under dagens 15 kilometer fristil på Beitostølen.
5 kilometer før mål sto kampen om seieren mellom Grøtting og Kristin Austgulen Fosnæs. Der var det altså Grøtting som til slutt trakk det lengste strået.
Grøtting stod over fredagens 10 kilometer på grunn av magesmerter i et forsøk på å spare seg til dagens distanse.
– Jeg er veldig glad for det nå, sier Grøtting til NRK etter målgang.
Skiskytter Ida Lien var dagens andre startende og gikk i mål til ledelse. Der ble hun værende til Grøtting overtok lederstolen.
Likevel holdt det til 3. plass for skiskytteren.
Heidi Weng vant fredagens 10 kilometer klassisk, men klarte ikke å gjenskape prestasjonen i dag. Allerede ved 6,2 kilometer hadde Weng 17 sekunder opp til teten.
Weng endte på 5. plass, 36 sekunder bak vinner.
Herrene skal ut på sin 15 kilometer klokken 13:00. Den kan du følge på NRK TV.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Selvik reddet straffe på overtid da Brest vant igjen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/selvik-reddet-straffe-pa-overtid-da-brest-vant-igjen-1.18086449</link>
      <description>Egil Selvik fortsetter å storspille i Brest-målet. Lørdag sikret han 1-0-seier borte mot Strasbourg ved å redde straffespark fem minutter på overtid.
Sraffen ble dømt etter en VAR-gjennomgang av en situasjon der ballen traff armen til Brest-spiller Mama Baldé, men det berget ikke hjemmelaget.
Brest tok ledelsen ved Noah Edjouma i det 22. minutt, etter en svak klarering av keeper Filip Jørgensen. Selvik forsvarte ledelsen med en rekke gode redninger og hjalp laget sitt til den tredje strake seieren i Ligue 1.
Selvik voktet Norges mål i nasjonsligaseieren over Wales for en uke siden, men han måtte overraskende sette seg på benken igjen da Norge knep gruppeseieren med 3-2-seier over Danmark i Parken tirsdag. Da var Ørjan Nyland tilbake i målet. Lørdag satt Nyland på benken for RB Leipzig.
Brest-seieren løftet laget til 6.-plass på tabellen. Strasbourg har bare tre lag bak seg på tabellen.
(©NTB)</description>

    <item>
      <title>Saudi-Arabia: Har skutt ned houthi-missiler</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/saudi-arabia_-har-skutt-ned-houthi-missiler-1.18086194</link>
      <description>Tre missiler som hadde retning mot Saudi-Arabias hovedstad Riyadh er skutt ned.
Det sier den saudiledede militærkoalisjonen, som er i en pågående væpnet konflikt med houthi-militsen.
I tillegg skal folk ha hørt flere eksplosjoner i Riyadh, melder Reuters.
Saudi-Arabia gikk til krig mot houthi-militsen i Jemen i 2015. Etter sju år med krig avtalte partene en våpenhvile i 2022.
I sommer har konflikten blusset opp igjen.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/historisk-_gta-6_-lansering_-solgte-for-nesten-4-milliarder-dollar-pa-en-dag-1.18086187</link>
      <description>Spillgiganten Rockstar Games knuser alle rekorder, melder Variety.
Allerede på lanseringsdagen omsatte «Grand Theft Auto 6», også kjent som «GTA 6», for 3,79 milliarder dollar.
Det tilsvarer over 37 milliarder norske kroner, og spillet forbigår dermed superheltfilmen «Avengers: End Game» som den største underholdningslanseringen noensinne.
«GTA 6» ble lansert torsdag på PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X og S, i tillegg til at det kan strømmes på Xbox One via Xbox Cloud Gaming.
I den sjette utgaven av actionspillet følger spillerne duoen Jason og Lucia mens de ufører ran og andre kriminelle oppdrag i den fiktive amerikanske delstaten Leonida.</description>

Two days into his new role, the Premier of B.C., Lorne Doerkson, issued a letter on Wednesday directing “ministries and central agencies to begin implementing a return-to-office plan for the BC Public Service.”

Doerkson continued his letter by highlighting that “public servants provide essential services that British Columbians rely on every day. Our government believes greater in-person collaboration will strengthen teamwork, mentorship, professional development and organizational culture while supporting strong service to the public.”

“I ask that you begin preparation for a phased return to the workplace, including a review of existing remote work arrangements, office capacity, and any accommodations that may be required. The goal should be to increase regular in-person attendance while maintaining government services and appropriate flexibility where needed,” the letter reads.

“Please provide my office with an update on proposed timelines, key implementation considerations and any policy, legal, or collective agreement issues that may need to be addressed.”

The premier ended by stating, “Our government is committed to a high-performing public service that delivers results for British Columbians. I am confident that increasing opportunities for employees to work together in person will help build a stronger, more effective public service.”

A raccoon is in the care of Wild ARC in Metchosin after her paw got stuck in a trap, resulting in it needing to be amputated.

Wild ARC says the nearby community was aware of the raccoon with her leg stuck in a trap for “some time,” but she had evaded all attempts to rescue her.

Her paw had become detached with the trap, leaving her with a severe injury and exposed bone.

“We don’t know exactly what kind of trap it was, but it clearly had a devastating impact,” said Ashley Currie, BC SPCA Wild ARC manager.

“There was exposed bone at the stump, and our primary concerns were infection and pain.”  

READ ALSO: BC SPCA warns drivers to watch for owls as daylight hours dwindle

The community members caught her and brought her to the Wild ARC team for emergency treatment.

“Raccoons are very resilient and can adapt well to being tripods,” said Currie. “Her stitches have been removed, and she has graduated to our outdoor enclosures to practice climbing.”

The team at Wild ARC estimates she will be at the centre for about a month or two to adapt, heal and regrow the fur at the surgical site before she can be released back to the wild.

Wild ARC says the raccoon’s story is a good reminder to follow best practices for managing conflicts with raccoons.

Best practices include using mild humane harassment, like placing lights at the den entrance or playing radio nearby. You can soak rags in apple cider vinegar, place them in a plastic container with holes poked in the lid and place the containers near den entry points.

BC SPCA says to wait to evict raccoons if they’re babies.

If a raccoon gets inside your home, you can also install a one-way door so the raccoons can leave but not enter. If that isn’t possible, they can be live-trapped and released immediately outside of the home and use reuniting techniques if there are babies present.

“Trapping and relocating wildlife away from their home is generally not a permanent or humane solution,” the SPCA says on an information page.

“Animals often injure themselves and may die trying to escape a trap. Relocated animals have to set up a new home, may starve trying to find food or get into fights with other animals over territory, and may spend vital energy trying to return home.”

The Canadian Food Inspection Agency has handed three grocery giants $10,000 fines each after it found produce inaccurately labelled as a Product of Canada.

The CFIA says Walmart, Loblaws and Pattison were each handed the fines on Oct. 22, after inspections earlier in the year, all relating to stores in Calgary.

“Food businesses are responsible for ensuring that all products they sell, whether made in Canada or imported, comply with Canada’s legislative requirements,” the CFIA said in an email to CHEK News.

“This includes ensuring that labels and advertisements are accurate, truthful, and do not mislead or deceive consumers.”

The food inspection agency says there were multiple labelling discrepancies found at the stores.

Pattison Food Group was the first to be inspected on March 27, following a complaint about inaccurate country-of-origin labels on pickles.

“While investigating the complaint, CFIA inspectors identified additional country-of-origin labelling discrepancies involving other products, including peppers and tomatoes, which contributed to the decision to issue a notice with penalty rather than a warning,” the CFIA said.

Loblaws was inspected on April 1 after a complaint about inaccurate country-of-origin labelling of tomatoes.

Similarly to the Pattison inspection, more inaccurate labels were found. At this store, the mislabelling was discovered on fresh produce including tomatoes, peppers, apples, eggplant, oranges and limes.

Walmart was also inspected on April 1 after a complaint about mandarins.

As with the other two, additional labelling discrepancies were found on other products, including apples, watermelon, pears, peppers, tomatoes, cucumbers, oranges, and onions.

“The CFIA selects appropriate compliance and enforcement actions based on a range of considerations including the degree of risk, the harm caused by the non-compliance, the compliance history of the regulated party, whether there is negligence or intent to violate federal requirements, and responsiveness to resolving the issue,” the email statement says.

The CFIA says for transparency, it shares enforcement actions on its website once they meet the requirements for public disclosure, and in some cases, they then get shared to X (formerly Twitter).

“It is important to note that certain enforcement actions, such as administrative monetary penalties, can span several months before there is an ultimate resolution,” the CFIA said.

The CFIA says that “Made in Canada” labels mean the last substantial transformation happened in Canada.

“For example, the processing of cheese, dough, sauce and other ingredients to create a pizza would be considered a substantial transformation,” the CFIA says on an information page about how to identify Canadian food.

“Whenever the ‘Made in Canada’ claim is used, it must also include a qualifying statement to indicate whether the food product is made in Canada from imported ingredients or a combination of imported and Canadian ingredients.”

If a label says it is “100% Canadian,” that means that all of the ingredients, processing and labour used to make the food were Canadian.

Nearly all British Columbians believe emergency risks are increasing, but a new BC Hydro survey suggests few households are fully prepared.

The survey found 92 per cent of residents believe emergency risks are on the rise, yet only 17 per cent say they have a complete 72-hour emergency kit at home.

The findings come after a series of powerful storms earlier this month caused outages affecting nearly half a million BC Hydro customers across the province. With more wind and heavy rain hitting parts of B.C., the utility providor is encouraging residents to prepare for future emergencies.

READ MORE: Evacuation alerts issued on Vancouver Island as weather warnings continue

“Our survey shows people understand the risks and many have already started preparing, but there is more work to do. Building a complete emergency kit and making a household plan are simple actions that can make a meaningful difference when an emergency occurs,” said BC Hydro spokesperson Whitney Deane in a release.

More than seven in 10 British Columbians reported taking at least one preparedness step in the past year, including storing additional food or drinking water (40 per cent), signing up for emergency alerts (35 per cent) and discussing emergency plans with household members (26 per cent).

Preparedness levels vary across the province. On Vancouver Island and the North Coast, 41 per cent of respondents had signed up for emergency alerts, while 20 per cent had completed emergency preparedness or first-aid training.

In the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley, despite 93 per cent recognizing the increasing risk of emergencies, only 28 per cent had signed up for emergency alerts and just 10 per cent had created or updated a household emergency plan.

BC Hydro is encouraging residents to assemble or refresh a 72-hour emergency kit with food, water, medications, flashlights, batteries and first-aid supplies.

Residents are also advised to create a household emergency plan, download the BC Hydro app and familiarize themselves with its outage map.

The utility reminds people to stay at least 10 metres away from downed or damaged power lines and call 911 to report them.

More information is available at bchydro.com/safety.
